source.title: An Adaptive Gradient Method with Energy and Momentum

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance of adaptive and momentum SGD methods on natural image-classification tasks, using optimizer comparisons rather than the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The paper tests optimizer generalization on natural-label image tasks. Its claims about other adaptive methods in the Introduction and cited literature are not extracted as results. No random-label capacity, width, architecture-bias, batch-size, dropout, sharpness-measure, or memorized-example-removal result is reported.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and momentum SGD using held-out image-classification accuracy under limited hyperparameter tuning, the same comparison method and measure as V4's original optimizer experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' stated conclusion: AEGDM accelerates AEGD and reduces its fluctuations, while achieving comparable or better generalization than SGDM and better generalization than Adam in their experiments. The discussion describes these results as showing the potential of energy-based adaptive methods.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a new energy-and-momentum optimizer with Adam and SGDM on natural-label image classification; it does not test random-label memorization or the other mapped interventions. It tunes only the base learning rate for each method in the reported comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: On CIFAR-10, the reported Adam-versus-SGDM generalization difference appears after the learning rate decays at epoch 150.
record.problems: The text gives qualitative optimizer comparisons but no exact Adam-versus-SGDM test-accuracy values or uncertainty estimates. Learning-rate tuning is limited to the base learning rate; results are on a small set of image-classification tasks and architectures.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying optimizer-comparison outcomes are stated numerically in prose; other plotted comparisons are not transcribed as exact results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and word-level language models. R1–R3 do not establish whether Adam's training performance equals or exceeds SGDM's.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable plotted values; the verdict therefore rests on the explicit CIFAR-10 prose. Additional plotted optimizer comparisons are declared omitted in rows_left_out. The CIFAR-100 prose describes performance as broadly similar but does not separately establish each Adam-versus-SGDM ordering. Table 1 also lists a VGG-16 SGDM learning rate of 0.03 and a SqueezeNet Adam rate of 0.003, neither included in the respective search grids stated in Section 5.2.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image networks.
Language benchmarks; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and its interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
